body.ab: began to feel that manner in which I sometimes anus'd myse;f with my gun was not without sin; for although I mostly preferr'd going alon, and while waiting in stillness for the coming of the fowl, my mind was at times so taken up in divine meditations, that the opportunities were seasons of instruction and comfort to me; yet, on other occasions, when accompanied by some of my acquaintances, and when no fowls appear'd which could be useful to us after being obtain'd, we sometimes, from wantonness or mere diversion, would destroy the small birds which could be of no service to us. This cruel procedure affects my heart while penning these lines.

body.p: In his 23d year Elias was married, by the Friends' ceremony, to Jemima Seaman. His wife was an only child; the parents were well off for common people, and at at their request the son-in-law mov'd home with them and carried on the farm—which at their decease became his own, and he liv'd there all his remaining life. Of his matrimonial part of his career, (it continued, and with unusual happiness, for 6058/ years,) he say, giving the account of his marriage:

On this important occasion, we felt the clear and consoling evidence of divine truth, and it remain'd with us as a seal upon our spirits, strengthnening us mutually to bear, with becoming fortitude, the vicissitudes and trials which fell to our lot, and of which we had a large share in passin through this probationary state. My wife, a;though not a very stong constitution, liv'd to be the mother of eleven children, four sons and seven daughterws. Our second daughter, a very lovely, promising child, died when young, with the small-pox, and the youngest ways not living at its birth. The rest all arriv'd to years of discretion, and afforded us considerable comfort, as they prov'd to be in a good degree dutiful children. All our sons, were of weak constitutions, and were not able to take care of themselves, being so enfeebl'd as not to be able to walk after the ninth or tenth year of their age. The two eldest died in the fifteenth year of their age, the third in his seventeenth year, and the youngest was nearly nineteen when he died. But, although thus helpless, the innocency of their lives, and the resign'd cheerfulness of their dispositions to their allotments, made the labor and toil of taking care of them agreeable and pleasant; and i trust we were preserv'd from murmuring or repinning, believing the dispensation to be in wisdom, and according to the will and gracious disposing of an all-wise providence, for purposes best known to hinself. And when I have observe'd the great anxiety and affliction which many parents have with undutiful children who are favor'd with health, especially their sons, I could perceive very few troubles and excercises, on that account, did not far exceed ours. The weakness and bodily infirmity of our sons tended to keep them much out of the way of troubles and temptations of the world; and we believ'd that in their death they were happy, and admitted into the realms of peace and joy: a reflection, the most comfortable and joyous that parents can have in regard to their tender offspring.
